newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: CBOT soybeans up in Asia on U.S. crush, Glencore.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans up in Asia on U.S. crush, Glencore.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soybean and soy product futures jumped in Asian trade on Friday on a bullish U.S. crushing report and news that a sale of Brazilian soybeans to the U.S. had fallen through, traders said.
At 0800 GMT the CBOT's May soybean contract was up 7.0 cents from Thursday's open outcry close at US$8.35 a bushel. May soymeal was $3.50 a ton higher at $269.50.
CBOT May corn futures also rose 3.0 cents a bushel to $3.0-3/4 in line with the gains in the soy complex.

Following the Chicago market's close, the U.S. National Oilseed Processors Association (NOPA) released a bullish report showing weekly crushing rates, as of March 12, rose to 30,106,000 bushels, up from 30,078,000 bushels the previous week and 25,892,000 bushels a year ago.
"We had expected the NOPA's crushing rates to fall in March due to active selling by Brazil," a Cheil futures trader said.
He said soybean prices had also been boosted by news that a a sale of 45,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans by trader Glencore to a U.S. firm had fallen through.
The previously reported sale had raised the prospect of U.S. suppliers losing market share at home to their South American competitor.
Seoul traders said South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) is likely to buy up to 40,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal through a tender later on Friday.
The NLCF invited tenders to buy up to 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for arrival by July 20 to the three South Korean ports of Inchon Kunsan and Ulsan.
